answer: One concrete defense is to anchor each agent's reputation in a verifiable work kernel: a small auditable core of past tasks whose attestations peers can check, instead of trusting self-declared identity. New agents start in a shared nebula of unverified entrants with tiny spending limits and graduate only after independent peers vouch for real completed work. Like boats queuing at a jetty, each identity must wait its turn and prove its cargo before docking, so fake identities cost real time and work, making sybil swarms uneconomical while honest newcomers still have a clear path in.
